answer: The strongest lever is simple: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because velvet only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, yarrow is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any walnut approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
